one_line_reason: Multiple human RCTs of oral D-aspartic acid on serum testosterone exist (the outcome it is marketed for); the single-ingredient trials found null/negative effects, which is itself worth central verification and consumer-facing accuracy.

selected.intervention: D-aspartic acid 6 g/day oral vs placebo, 12 weeks, alongside supervised resistance training
selected.primary_outcome: basal total and free testosterone, plus strength/muscle measures
selected.why_selected: Longest-duration single-ingredient RCT directly testing DAA's marketed claim (testosterone increase) in a general athletic population; found a reduction in testosterone with DAA

selected.intervention: D-aspartic acid 3 g/day oral vs placebo, 2-week crossover with washout
selected.primary_outcome: serum testosterone and hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis biomarkers
selected.why_selected: Single-ingredient, crossover-controlled human trial on the same marketed outcome (testosterone), general athletic population

selected.population: male boxers undergoing 11 days of nocturnal normobaric hypoxia exposure (n=16)
selected.intervention: D-aspartic acid 6 g/day oral vs control, 14 days, during simulated-altitude training
selected.why_selected: Another single-ingredient RCT on testosterone; included for completeness though the hypoxia-training context is a blocker

selected.intervention: 2660 mg D-aspartic acid + 200 mg ubiquinol + 10 mg zinc, once daily, 3 months, vs placebo
selected.dose_as_stated: 2660 mg D-aspartic acid (combined with ubiquinol and zinc)
selected.primary_outcome: semen parameters (progressive motility) and serum testosterone
selected.why_selected: Most recent human RCT with a positive signal, but it is a 3-ingredient combination product and a clinical infertility population, not a clean single-ingredient exposure

blockers: 40248985 is a 3-component combination product (DAA + ubiquinol + zinc) in a clinical infertility population, not a single-ingredient general-use exposure
38201906 studies DAA specifically under a nocturnal normobaric hypoxia/altitude-training protocol, not ordinary supplement use

The systematic review (37697053) covers 27 different 'testosterone booster' ingredients pooled together; only 2 of its 52 included studies are D-aspartic acid, so it cannot be cited as DAA-specific evidence

excluded_pmids.reason: Broad systematic review of 27 different testosterone-booster ingredients (D-aspartic acid is only 2 of 52 included studies); not DAA-specific primary evidence, though it corroborates the null pattern
Anti-androgen drugs for OCD; unrelated to D-aspartic acid, evidently indexed on an unrelated term match
Timing of anti-seizure treatment in status epilepticus; mentions NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartic acid) receptors, not D-aspartic acid supplementation
YMDD motif mutation in hepatitis B virus; 'aspartic acid' appears only as part of the amino-acid mutation code, unrelated substance/context
Meta-analysis of preemptive analgesia including NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartic acid) receptor antagonist drugs; not D-aspartic acid supplementation
Esketamine (an NMDA receptor antagonist drug) for postoperative fatigue; unrelated to D-aspartic acid supplement
Esketamine for anesthesia induction in elderly patients; unrelated to D-aspartic acid supplement
tDCS effect on cortical NMDA neurotransmission measured via auditory response; unrelated to D-aspartic acid supplementation
